_meta.purpose: Beat-locked generation unit plan for the LOCAL open-weight rebuild of the 43.000 s / 1290-frame vertical reel. Defines the 14 independent image-to-video generation units, their exact frame budgets through the HunyuanVideo 1.5 -> RIFE x5 -> decimate-to-30 chain, and the three beat-placed split points.
_meta.character_policy: Leads are addressed by code only (M1, F1); sets by code only (SET_A, SET_B); corps as corps_A / corps_B. No real person's name and no named TV character appears anywhere in this file, and no banned token appears in any descriptive, prompt-bearing or generated field. The only matches a token grep can produce are inside repository FILE PATHS, which are part of the existing directory layout and are never copied into a prompt. Regenerating prompts from this file must still pass the token gate at 05_build/bin/ipgate.sh.
_meta.identity_rule: Every still built from a unit in this file copies consistency_anchors.<code>.verbatim_block byte-for-byte and keeps consistency_anchors.ordering_rule clause order: identity -> wardrobe -> props/posture -> action -> set -> light -> lens -> grade.
_meta.open_conflict_flagged: identity_sheet cross_scene_rules says neither lead wears a hat in any scene (hats belong to the corps); shot_bible dresses M1 in a fedora for macro shots 08 and 09. Unresolved, out of scope for this plan, but it must be settled before the SET_B stills are generated.

timebase.chain: HunyuanVideo15ImageToVideo N frames @24 -> FrameInterpolate(multiplier=5) -> (N-1)*5+1 frames @120 -> keep every 4th -> 30 fps -> trim tail to target_frames_30fps
timebase.timebase_note: RIFE x5 then keep-every-4th is a pure 24->30 fps conversion: wall-clock duration and motion speed are unchanged. The surplus frames are genuine extra CONTENT at the tail, not a speed change.

window_authority.rule: Unit boundaries are FRAME boundaries at 30 fps, taken from the ffprobe-measured per-clip frame counts (68/88/114/85/78/145/187/134/178/48/165 = 1290).
window_authority.why: tech_ground_truth doc_claims_checked marks the per-shot SECONDS column in the report/shot table as DISAGREES (frame-quantised boundaries drift up to +24 ms) and rules 'authoritative: frame counts, not seconds'. shot_bible's dur_s values (e.g. 6.240 / 5.920 / 5.504 for shots 07/09/11) are those drifting seconds; the frame-exact values are 6.233333 / 5.933333 / 5.500000.
window_authority.consequence: Because every unit boundary is an integer frame and every macro shot's frame count is split into two integers, the 14 target frame counts sum to exactly 1290 by construction. No rounding residue had to be absorbed anywhere.

beat_grid_used.phase_offset_justification: No phase had to be ASSUMED: beat_grid ships the measured 69-entry beats_s array, so the grid is used as given rather than re-derived. Its phase is first_beat_s = 0.2612 s and its spacing 0.627778 s (60/95.575 = 0.6277792). The array is self-consistent with that phase to under 0.1 ms across all 69 beats (0.2612 + 68*0.627778 = 42.95009 vs the listed 42.9501), so the derived grid and the measured grid are the same grid.
beat_grid_used.confidence_handling: MEDIUM, with 191.41 BPM scoring 0.4233 against the winner's 0.4411. Treated per the file's own ruling: 95.575 and 191.15 are ONE grid at two subdivisions, so every beat is also a 191 grid point and a cut on a beat is safe under either reading. Half-beat points are used only where the nearest-grid rule selects one (macro shot 11), and that seam is deliberately hidden as a continuation rather than shown as a cut - so if the double-tempo reading is wrong, nothing visible is riding on it.
beat_grid_used.grid_vs_existing_edit: Only 1 of the 11 existing cloud cuts lands within +-80 ms of this grid; the cloud edit was cut to shot content, not to the music. The three NEW seams introduced here are the first cuts in the piece that are actually beat-placed.

sub_unit_delta.choice: (i) camera/angle change - 07A and 07B are different setups of the same staging

sub_a.framing: eye-level locked-off waist-up TWO-SHOT, both torsos and the riser line readable, M1 screen-right of F1
sub_a.content: the charmed exchange and M1's smooth backward lean onto the riser behind him; closes with his weight settled back, jacket open, hands still low
sub_a.opening_still: fresh still generated for this unit

sub_b.framing: tighter eye-level SINGLE on M1, chest-up, F1's near shoulder and cheek held soft in the left foreground, corps bank compressed behind
sub_b.content: corps unison bounce on the bar line, then the raised index finger wagging toward the lens; the gesture now owns the frame
sub_b.opening_still: fresh still generated for this unit - deliberately a NEW size and eyeline, not a resume of 07A's last frame

why: The punctuation gesture of the whole studio half (the finger wag) sits 1.63 s inside 07B. A size change on the beat gives it its own setup and makes the seam read as an edit rather than a stutter.
A same-size restart of the same two-shot is the exact failure the brief warns about: identical framing plus a fresh latent equals a visible pose pop.
It also discharges shot_bible AB-01(b): corps unison no longer has to match ACROSS the seam, because the corps changes scale at the seam anyway.
No camera MOVE is invented (shot_bible CAM-01) - both halves stay locked off. Only the setup changes, which a split into two independent i2v generations forces regardless.
sub_unit_delta.risk: Identity drift between two independently generated stills of the same face at two sizes. Mitigation: copy consistency_anchors.M1.verbatim_block byte-for-byte into both, honour consistency_anchors.ordering_rule, and use 07A's rendered last frame as one of the Flux.2 reference Figures when building 07B's still.

sub_unit_delta.choice: (i) camera/angle change - the signature gesture gets its own setup

sub_a.framing: low-angle medium, sandstone and bleached sky above; this half carries the reel's ONLY camera move - the lateral pan riding the wrist snaps
sub_a.content: wrist-snap accents on the pan, then the elbow-pump groove one pump per beat; closes with elbows back and weight loaded
sub_a.opening_still: fresh still generated for this unit

sub_b.framing: harder, lower, tighter frontal medium - arms and hands dominant, gate frame centred behind the head, LOCKED OFF (pan ends at the cut)
sub_b.content: the double-point: both index fingers punched straight into the lens at full extension, then the lateral arm whip out of it
sub_b.opening_still: fresh still generated for this unit - a new angle, and the single hardest still in the build (ten unambiguous digits, foreshortened)

why: The cut lands on a DOWNBEAT (32.9057 s, bar line) - the strongest possible place in the bar to change setup, and only 27.6 ms off the natural midpoint.
Isolating the pan in 09A means the locked-off 09B can be judged on hand quality alone; mixing a pan into the double-point would smear the fingers that are already the riskiest geometry in the reel.
A hard angle drop on the bar line reads as an edit deliberately punching in on the gesture.
sub_unit_delta.restaging_note: In the cloud edit the double-point sat 3.4 s into the whole shot, i.e. ~0.47 s into 09B. Re-stage it to land on the next beat, 33.5334 s = 0.633 s into 09B, so the point hits a beat instead of arriving mid-air off an opening still.
sub_unit_delta.risk: Sun direction, hat/mask silhouettes and gate-frame placement must match across the seam. Mitigation: build 09B's still from 09A's rendered last frame plus the SET_B plate as Flux.2 reference Figures.

sub_unit_delta.choice: (ii) continuation - 11B's opening still IS 11A's closing frame

sub_a.framing: eye-level waist-up hero medium, M1 right of centre
sub_a.content: the slow swaggering wrist rotation; ends with the hand just settled and the body already decelerating - near-static by design
sub_a.opening_still: fresh still generated for this unit

sub_b.framing: IDENTICAL framing, lens, light and screen position - nothing about the camera changes
sub_b.content: the faint closed-mouth smirk forms, then everything decelerates into the locked statue that must be rock-still through frame 1289
sub_b.opening_still: the LAST RENDERED FRAME of 11A, extracted and fed in as this unit's i2v start image (and as a Flux.2 reference Figure if the still is re-cleaned)

why: This is the outro. The shot's whole job is one unbroken stare decelerating to a dead stop; a visible cut 2.87 s from the end would restart the deceleration and undercut the freeze.

It is also the only one of the three seams NOT on a main beat - it sits on the half-beat of the 191.15 subdivision, 124.9 ms from the midpoint. A seam you are hiding does not need a bar line under it, which is exactly why the nearest-grid-point rule is safe to follow here.

Continuation is cheapest to make invisible precisely here: 11A ends in deceleration, so its last frame is motion-blur-free and makes a clean i2v start image. The same trick would fail at the 07 and 09 seams, where the body is mid-beat.
shot_bible is explicit that nothing may be trimmed off this tail - the 43.000 s lock lives on 11B's last frame. Keeping the seam invisible keeps that obligation inside one continuous performance.
sub_unit_delta.risk: Colour/contrast step at the seam from two decode passes. Mitigation: extract 11A's last frame as PNG (not a re-encoded JPEG), and grade 11A and 11B as one pair at assembly.

verification.headroom_warning: Every unit clears its target, but the native headroom is 1-5 frames (0.033-0.167 s). shot_bible TRIM-01 asks for ~0.2 s of slack at EACH end to discard the model's opening latent freeze. Use recommended_N_with_trim01_slack (a +6-frame budget) if that lead-in trim is wanted; unit 06 is the only one where that budget hits the 121-frame ceiling, and it still lands exactly 0.200 s of slack.
verification.cost_note: 14 units at roughly 18-19 min per 5 s generation, scaled by duration, is on the order of 11-12 GPU-hours for one full pass of the video stage alone - before RIFE and before any reroll.
